_editorial: HAND-AUTHORED. Never written by a script. Figures quoted from open data carry the dataset they came from so every number on the rendered page traces to sources.json.
title: A public running hub near Champ-de-Mars
title_fr: Un point d'appui pour la course à pied près du Champ-de-Mars
status_note: Research only. Nothing has been submitted to anyone. The adverse precedent below is being investigated first.
summary: Secure storage, drinking water, and basic changing facilities for runners using the Champ-de-Mars and Invalides lawns, tested as a 12-month pilot before anything permanent is built.

problem.statement: The Champ-de-Mars and the Esplanade des Invalides are among the most heavily used running surfaces in Paris. Neither has anywhere to leave a bag, refill a bottle reliably in winter, or change. Runners either carry everything or do not come.
problem.who_is_affected: Residents and workers in the 7e who run before or after work, and visitors staying nearby.
problem.evidence_available: None that counts runners. See evidence_limits.

proposal.description: A bank of secure lockers and, later, somewhere to change, on a side allee of the Champ-de-Mars. Nothing dug, nothing plumbed, nothing that cannot be removed. It closes the one gap the site actually has.
proposal.one_line: Paris has already built the water and the toilets here. What is missing is somewhere to put your bag.

components.why: The single most named gap by runners in Seoul's own consultation, and the only element that needs no service connection of any kind.
Answers the beginner's question, which is where to go rather than how to run. Seoul put route maps on its media board for the same reason.
Changing was the second gap Seoul's runners named. Accessible from the start, not retrofitted.

components.what: Two showers and clothes spin dryers
components.why: What makes running before work possible rather than theoretical. Seoul included spin dryers specifically; they are cheap and they are the difference between carrying wet kit to the office or not.

deliberately_excluded.why: 19 already exist in the Champ-de-Mars box, 18 available, three on the preferred allee. Asking for one would suggest the proposal had not checked.
7 sanisettes already serve this site, all wheelchair accessible, several 06h00-22h00.
It converts a park amenity into a commercial occupation with a slower permission track. Kept as a separate later proposal.
No delivered precedent there and five abandoned projects.

deliberately_excluded.what: Any excavation, foundation or tree removal
deliberately_excluded.why: Removes the most likely heritage objection at tier 1.

proposal.reversibility: Tier 1 is ballasted, not founded. It can be lifted out in a day and the removal cost is inside the pilot budget.

location.method: Every 7e-local Budget Participatif project sited at Champ-de-Mars was checked against its outcome. Three were delivered and five abandoned. The split does not follow cost, edition or piloting Direction. It follows exact position: everything delivered sits on a side allee, everything abandoned was proposed on the central axis.

Reamenagement des allees du Champ de Mars
Creation aire de petanque et bancs ecologiques

abandoned_on_the_central_axis.project: Jardin pedagogique sur le Champ de Mars
Parcours de sante au Champ de Mars
Panneaux Histoire du Champ de mars
Une ruche sur le Champ de Mars

evidence.caveat: Eight data points and no recorded reasons. This is a hypothesis strong enough to site a pilot on, not a finding strong enough to state as fact in a submission.

candidates.label: Allee Adrienne-Lecouvreur
candidates.case: The petanque court and eco benches were approved here from the 2016 edition at EUR 40,000 and built. That is a delivered precedent for a small new recreational installation at this exact address, piloted by the same Direction that would pilot this one. Three drinking fountains are already on this allee.
candidates.risk: None specific to the site beyond the general heritage question, which tier 1 avoids by needing no foundation.

candidates.label: Avenue Charles Risler
candidates.case: Four drinking fountains and a sanisette open 06h00-22h00. The EUR 2,000,000 restoration of the paths, lawns, kerbs and fencing was addressed here and delivered.
candidates.risk: A site that has just received a EUR 2,000,000 heritage restoration may be the least willing to accept a new object on it.

candidates.label: Allee Thomy-Thierry
candidates.case: Two drinking fountains and a sanisette open 06h00-22h00. The EUR 600,000 allees project was delivered here.
candidates.risk: Same as above, at smaller scale.

explicitly_avoided.why: Three of the five abandoned Champ-de-Mars projects were sited here, including the fitness trail that is the direct precedent for this proposal. Proposing the same thing at the same address is the one move guaranteed to fail.
No delivered precedent for a new installation anywhere on the axis.

cost_tiers.scope: A bank of 20 secure outdoor lockers with phone-based access, on a ballasted plinth needing no foundation, plus signage. No plumbing, no power beyond the access system, nothing dug.

line_items.item: 20-locker outdoor bank, code or QR access

cost_tiers.why_this_tier: Costs less than the EUR 40,000 petanque court and eco benches that was approved and delivered on Allee Adrienne-Lecouvreur from the 2016 edition. That is the closest precedent at this site and it is a built one.
cost_tiers.estimate_basis: Order-of-magnitude estimate made for this record. Not a quotation. Firmed up by asking the piloting Direction for a costing before submission.

cost_tiers.scope: Tier 1 plus two demountable changing cubicles with bench, hooks, mirror and light, and 20 further lockers. Power connection required. Still no water connection.

line_items.item: Two demountable changing cubicles, wheelchair accessible

cost_tiers.why_this_tier: Changing was the specific gap Seoul's runners named. This is the first tier that closes it.
cost_tiers.estimate_basis: Order-of-magnitude estimate made for this record. Not a quotation. Firmed up by asking the piloting Direction for a costing before submission.

cost_tiers.scope: Tier 2 plus two showers, hot water, and clothes spin dryers. Requires a water supply and a drainage connection, which is where most of the cost sits and where most of the permitting risk sits.

line_items.item: Water supply and drainage connection to the existing network
Two showers, wheelchair accessible, with electric hot water
Contingency, 10 percent, on new items only

cost_tiers.why_this_tier: Matches what Seoul actually built. Note the drainage connection alone is roughly the cost of the entire tier 1 three times over, which is the honest reason to phase rather than ask for this first.
cost_tiers.estimate_basis: Order-of-magnitude estimate made for this record. Not a quotation. Firmed up by asking the piloting Direction for a costing before submission.

scale_context.the_wrong_denominator: Comparing this pilot to the arrondissement's own investment budget makes it look enormous. That comparison is misleading and this page no longer leads with it.
scale_context.why_it_is_misleading: The etat special d'arrondissement is an operating budget for the buildings the mairie runs. Its 2023 expenditure is electricity at EUR 332,401, premises cleaning at EUR 175,850, water at EUR 115,738, district heating at EUR 102,414, canteen food at EUR 122,650. Its entire investment section is a single line, Dotation d'investissement versee, EUR 161,405. Nothing physical in the 7e is built from it at any size.

per_resident.residents_source: INSEE legal population via geo.api.gouv.fr, commune 75107
per_resident.ratio: The Ville de Paris invests about 372 times more per resident than the arrondissement's own investment line amounts to per resident of the 7e.
per_resident.reading: EUR 3.36 per resident per year is not what Paris spends on the 7e. It is the size of the arrondissement council's own discretionary capital allocation. The real money is on the citywide budget and is spent in the 7e by city Directions.

the_right_denominators.benchmark: The petanque court and eco benches delivered on Allee Adrienne-Lecouvreur
the_right_denominators.reading: Tier 1 at EUR 28,000 costs less than something already approved and built at the preferred site.

the_right_denominators.benchmark: Budget Participatif money attached to live 7e projects in the 2025 edition alone
the_right_denominators.reading: Tier 1 is about 1.5 percent of it.
Tier 1 is about half a percent of what this mechanism has already built here.
Tier 1 is about one millionth of it.

scale_context.conclusion: Against the mechanism that would actually fund it, this is a small ask. It only looks large against a budget that would never have paid for it.

target_mechanism.why: It is the only route in the 7e that moves capital sums of this size. The comparison that follows is rendered from the section's own pipeline data, deduplicated to project level, and is never split by avancement: a project whose operations sit at different stages is counted under each of those stages, so status figures cannot be added.

alternatives_considered.mechanism: Direction budget, outside any participatory process
alternatives_considered.verdict: Possible but opaque from outside. Kept as a fallback if the Budget Participatif route fails.

secondary_delegations: propreté, environnement, espaces verts et mobilité
elu.why_no_name: The élus dataset was last modified 2021-12-01 and predates the March 2026 municipal elections. No holder is named here until the mairie du 7e site has been checked. See the Blocking Preconditions in the section spec.

direction.likely: Direction des Espaces Verts et de l’Environnement
direction.basis: Sport has 5 operations in the 7e, exactly the sample floor. The theme-level inference on the Power page names Direction de la Jeunesse et des Sports (3 of 5). This proposal names Direction des Espaces Verts et de l’Environnement instead, on the 2 operations the author judges park-sited (Parcours de santé au Champ de Mars, Gym douce dans les espaces verts). n=2 is below the floor, park-sited is an editorial classification with no field behind it, and the outdoor Parcours sportif 2,3 km went to Direction de la Jeunesse et des Sports. Treat both Directions as open.
direction.alternative: Direction de la Voirie et des Déplacements, if the site ends up outside the park.

conseil_de_quartier.why: The candidate sites sit in these two quartiers. Entry through the conseil de quartier is also what the délégation conseils de quartier et associations exists for.

funding_cycle.note: Both dates are unverified. Nothing is submitted against a date that has not been checked.

adverse_precedent.headline: A publicly voted fitness trail at Champ-de-Mars was approved and then abandoned.

direct_precedent.titre_projet_gagnant: Parcours de santé au Champ de Mars
direct_precedent.direction_pilote_projet: Direction des Espaces Verts et de l’Environnement
direct_precedent.why_it_matters: This is the same idea, at the same site, already funded by public vote, and it did not get built. Any proposal for a running facility at Champ-de-Mars that does not confront this will be dismissed by anyone who knows the file.

other_abandoned_champ_de_mars_projects.titre_projet_gagnant: Jardin pédagogique sur le Champ de Mars
Une ruche sur le Champ de Mars
Panneaux Histoire du Champ de mars

adverse_precedent.pattern: Five abandoned 7e-local projects are sited at Champ-de-Mars, together 134,500 EUR of the 309,500 EUR of 7e-local money attached to abandoned projects. Five out of the seven abandoned local projects are at one site.
adverse_precedent.reasons_recorded_in_data: None. The dataset records the abandonment and not the cause.

hypothesis.text: Champ-de-Mars is a site classé, so physical installations require heritage approval.
hypothesis.rule: This is a hypothesis and is not stated as fact on any page or in any proposal until it is verified against a primary source. Until then the page reports the pattern and declines to explain it.

adverse_precedent.consequence_for_this_proposal: The first research task is establishing why those five projects died. The answer decides whether the pilot names a Champ-de-Mars location at all, or deliberately sites itself just outside the protected perimeter.

supporting_precedent.name: Runner Station, Yeouinaru Station, Seoul
supporting_precedent.what: A municipal facility built into unused space inside a metro station on Line 5, on the B1 and M1 floors, opened 21 May 2024. It carries 42 lockers, changing rooms, powder rooms, shoe sanitisers, body-composition measurement, and a media board showing weather and running conditions. Entry is free and access is by phone authentication. Open 06:00 to 24:00.
supporting_precedent.revenue_model: Entry free; lockers charged by size and duration, roughly KRW 2,200 to 6,100 for four hours. Running crews get free use of the space. Clothing rental is paid.
supporting_precedent.stated_rationale: The city frames it as converting idle station space into everyday sport and leisure facilities, citing roughly 8.83 million runners nationally as of 2022.
supporting_precedent.evidence_it_worked: Seoul announced an expansion on 23 October 2025 to three further stations: Gwanghwamun (Line 5), Hoehyeon (Line 4) and World Cup Stadium (Line 6). A separate facility at Ttukseom Station opens free public showers.
supporting_precedent.capital_cost_note: Not published in the English-language sources checked. The cost tiers on this page are Paris estimates and are not derived from Seoul.
supporting_precedent.relevance: The model is repurposing unused indoor transit space, not building on parkland. That is a materially different proposition from a structure on the Champ-de-Mars lawn, and in Paris it would fall to RATP and Ile-de-France Mobilites rather than to the Ville de Paris. It is recorded here as a second route, not as a demand figure for Paris.
supporting_precedent.not_evidence_of: Demand for a running facility in the 7e. Seoul's usage says nothing about Paris.

metrics.note: No baseline exists. The pilot creates the first measurement.

metrics.method: Incident log kept by the operating Direction
Actual spend against the maintenance line
Days with all lockers and the fountain in service, over days in the period
Short on-site survey at months 6 and 12

evaluation.decision_rule: At month 12 the numbers decide: continue, move the site, or remove the installation and publish what it cost.

maintenance_plan.who: Named at submission. The proposal does not leave maintenance to be worked out later, because unowned maintenance is how small installations become abandoned ones.
maintenance_plan.annual_cost_estimate_note: Not estimated yet. It is estimated before submission, not after.
consumables: Locker mechanism batteries or card system
maintenance_plan.end_of_life: The pilot tier is demountable and its removal cost is part of the pilot budget.

evidence_limits: No runner count exists for the Champ-de-Mars or the Invalides esplanade, in any dataset checked. Nothing on this page claims measured demand.
The bike counters at Pont des Invalides are shown as an active-mobility proxy and labelled as one. They count bicycles. They are not evidence of demand for a running facility.
The Budget Participatif dataset records that projects were abandoned, never why. The siting hypothesis rests on eight data points and no stated reasons.
Every cost figure on this page is an order-of-magnitude estimate made for this record. None is a quotation, and none has been checked against a Direction.
The locker revenue model is entirely assumed. Utilisation, session length and the share of paying uses are guesses shown so they can be challenged.
Winter operation of the drinking fountains is not recorded in the dataset. Water is confirmed available now, not in February.
open_questions: Why were the five Champ-de-Mars Budget Participatif projects abandoned? Primary source required.
Does the site classé status of the Champ-de-Mars apply to demountable installations?
Who currently holds the délégation Culture, sports et santé at the mairie du 7e, post-2026 elections?
Which Direction would own maintenance at each candidate site?

status_log.detail: While building the section's abandoned-projects file, found that Parcours de santé au Champ de Mars (40,000 EUR, edition 2016, identifiant_projet_gagnant 2357) won a Budget Participatif vote and is recorded as ABANDONNÉ, along with four other Champ-de-Mars projects totalling 94,500 EUR. This is directly adverse to this proposal and is now its first research task. No siting decision is made until the reason is established.

status_log.what: Tested whether the Champ-de-Mars abandonment pattern is fatal. It is not. Of 8 Champ-de-Mars 7e-local projects, 3 were delivered (EUR 2,640,000) and 5 abandoned (EUR 134,500). A EUR 40,000 petanque court with benches from the same 2016 edition, same piloting Direction, was built on Allee Adrienne-Lecouvreur.
status_log.hypothesis: The split appears to follow exact location, not cost, edition or Direction: everything abandoned was proposed on the central axis (Avenue Joseph Bouvard, Rue Savorgnan de Brazza), everything delivered sits on a side allee (Adrienne-Lecouvreur, Thomy-Thierry, Charles Risler). Eight data points, no recorded reasons. Unverified.
status_log.consequence: Siting the pilot on a side allee, with the petanque court as the cited precedent, is the first option to test.
status_log.outcome: Open. Needs a primary source on why the central-axis projects were dropped.

status_log.what: Sourced the Seoul Runner Station precedent from Seoul Metropolitan Government material. Recorded in supporting_precedent with four source URLs.
status_log.consequence: Seoul's model is unused indoor transit space, not parkland. In Paris that route runs through RATP and Ile-de-France Mobilites, not the Ville de Paris, so it is a separate proposal with separate routing.
status_log.outcome: Open. Capital cost not published in the sources checked.

status_log.what: Tested the Seine quai as a site. Found project 11141, Favoriser la pratique du sport dans le 7e, EUR 500,000, 2023 edition, piloted by the Direction de la Jeunesse et des Sports. Two of its three operations have not started and carry no stage dates: Renovation du Parcours sportif 2,3 km at 23 Quai Anatole France, and De nouveaux equipements legers pour faire du sport en plein air.
status_log.consequence: The first approach should be a question about an existing funded project, not a proposal for a new one. This also relocates the routing to the Direction de la Jeunesse et des Sports and the conseil de quartier Invalides.
status_log.outcome: Open. Needs the current status of operations 7788 and 8023 from the Direction.

status_log.what: Traced where Budget Participatif money physically sits. It becomes an autorisation de programme labelled BPA - Direction - arrondissement. Sport lines exist for at least ten arrondissements. The 7e has no DJS line for 2018 to 2022, but that dataset ends at 2022 and cannot cover the 2023 edition.
status_log.consequence: Gives a named budget line to ask about, BPA - DJS - 7e arrondissement, rather than a vague question about funding. Also found that the parcours sportif already exists in a derelict state, so the ask is restoration rather than new build.
status_log.outcome: Open. Five specific questions recorded for the Direction de la Jeunesse et des Sports.

status_log.what: Confirmed against the Mairie du 7e's own Budget Participatif 2023 page that project 11141 combines three separate resident proposals, and identified which operation each became.
status_log.consequence: The one delivered operation is the seniors and gentle-exercise idea, piloted by Espaces Verts. Both unstarted operations are the running-specific ideas, piloted by the Direction de la Jeunesse et des Sports. The proposal now has a precise account of what was promised and what was not done.
status_log.outcome: Verified against a primary source. Supersedes the earlier search-derived description.

site_infrastructure._why_this_matters: Two of the four things a running facility needs are already built at this site, at public expense. Asking for them again would weaken the proposal and inflate its cost. The ask is narrowed to what is genuinely missing.
site_infrastructure.consequence: The proposal asks for lockers, changing and washing only. It does not ask for water or toilets, and says on its face that both already exist and were already paid for.
site_infrastructure.note_on_provenance: Counts on this page are read from the generated site-context file, not typed into this record, so they cannot drift from the source.
site_infrastructure.water_open_question: The dataset records current availability, not winter operation. Whether these park fountains run year-round is unconfirmed and must be checked before the proposal claims water is available in February.
site_infrastructure.toilets_note: The 06h00-22h00 sanisette hours are a natural operating window for the facility, and match Seoul’s 06:00-24:00 locker hours closely enough to adopt.

usage.note: No count of runners at Champ-de-Mars exists in any dataset checked. Nobody has measured this, which is itself part of the argument for a pilot.
usage.first_real_measurement: Locker unlock counts in month one of the pilot produce the first actual count of runners using a facility in the 7e. That measurement is an output of the pilot, not an input to it.
usage.proxy_warning: This is not evidence of demand for a running facility. It counts bicycles at Pont des Invalides, and is never presented as a runner count. What it does establish is that this corridor carries heavy self-powered traffic every day of the year.

locker_model.principle: Free to use for the length of a run. Charged only beyond that. The pricing exists to ration lockers and offset maintenance, not to make money.
locker_model.why_not_full_charging: Charging properly for lockers on public parkland turns a park amenity into a commercial occupation, which requires an autorisation d'occupation temporaire and a different, slower permission track. Keeping the first two hours free keeps the pilot inside the amenity regime it is easiest to approve under.

proposed_tariff.rationale: Covers a normal run with time either side. The overwhelming majority of uses should pay nothing.
Discourages using a public locker as day storage.
Bounds the worst case so the tariff cannot read as a fine.

locker_model.access: Phone-based, code or QR, no staffed desk. This is what lets the facility open 06h00-22h00 without 16 hours of staffing, and it is the mechanism Seoul uses.
locker_model.seoul_comparison: Seoul charges from the first minute: roughly KRW 2,200 to 6,100 for four hours by locker size, more at weekends, with entry to the space free. The model here is deliberately gentler because the permission regime differs.

revenue_model._status: MODELLED, NOT OBSERVED. Every figure below is an assumption. They are shown so the arithmetic can be challenged, and the pilot exists to replace them with measurements.
revenue_model.conclusion: Roughly the order of the estimated annual maintenance. The tariff is a maintenance offset, not a business case, and the proposal should say so rather than dress it up as revenue.

phasing.recommendation: Ask for tier 1. Ask for tiers 2 and 3 as named options in the same document, conditional on what tier 1 measures.
phasing.why: Tier 1 is the only tier that costs less than a comparable installation already approved and built on this exact site. It needs no excavation, no drainage and no permanent foundation, which removes the heritage objection that most plausibly killed the earlier Champ-de-Mars projects. It is also the only tier that can be removed without trace if it fails.
phasing.escalation_rule: Tier 2 is requested only if tier 1's measured locker use exceeds a threshold agreed in advance with the piloting Direction. Tier 3 is requested only if tier 2 is used and a drainage route has been confirmed as feasible.

vending.recommendation: Keep vending out of the pilot. Propose it separately, later.
vending.why: A vending machine on public parkland is a commercial occupation, not a park amenity. It needs an autorisation d'occupation temporaire and, depending on scale, a concession procedure. That is a slower and more contested permission track than the one lockers sit on, and attaching it to the pilot exposes the whole proposal to it.
vending.what_covers_the_need_now: The drinking fountains already in the Champ-de-Mars study area, counted in site-context.json. Free. Hydration, which is the thing a runner actually needs mid-run, is already solved at this site.
if_pursued_later: Attach it to an existing kiosk concession rather than installing a standalone machine, so it runs on a permission that already exists.
Price it as an amenity, not a captive-audience concession. A tariff cap should be written into the proposal rather than left to the operator.
Bring it as its own proposal record with its own routing, since the deciding Direction is unlikely to be the same one.
vending.note_on_the_reference: East Asian station vending works because it sits inside a transit concession estate with dense footfall and an established operator. The Paris equivalent of that setting is a metro station, not a park lawn, which points at the second proposal route rather than this one.

live_project_to_attach_to._why_this_matters: There is already voted, approved sport money in the 7e whose delivery has stalled, and one of its stalled operations is a sports trail on the Seine quai. Attaching to that is a far shorter route than winning a new Budget Participatif project.

live_project_to_attach_to.inconsistency_to_check: The project is recorded as LIVRAISON at project level while two of its three operations show no start date at any stage. Either the remaining operations are still to come, or the project was closed with them undelivered. The dataset does not say which, and this is the first question to ask.
live_project_to_attach_to.what_it_supports: The Champ-de-Mars parcours de santé was abandoned in 2016. The same idea was funded again in 2023 at a different site, on the quai. That is evidence for the siting hypothesis: the idea was acceptable, the location was not.
live_project_to_attach_to.recommended_first_move: Do not open by proposing a new facility. Open by asking the Direction de la Jeunesse et des Sports what the status of operations 7788 and 8023 is, and whether lockers and changing could be scoped into the parcours sportif renovation that is already funded. A resident helping an approved project move is a different conversation from a resident asking for a new one.

what_changes_if_this_route_is_taken.direction: Direction de la Jeunesse et des Sports, not Direction des Espaces Verts et de l’Environnement.
what_changes_if_this_route_is_taken.quartier: Conseil de quartier Invalides, not Gros Caillou.
what_changes_if_this_route_is_taken.mechanism: An existing 2023 Budget Participatif project, not a new edition.
what_changes_if_this_route_is_taken.money: Potentially none new. The tier 1 cost sits inside an unspent EUR 500,000 envelope.

where_the_money_sits.mechanism: Budget Participatif money becomes an autorisation de programme on the Ville investment budget, tagged by Direction and arrondissement. The destination labels run BPA - <Direction> - <arrondissement>, for example BPA - DJS - 13e arrondissement.
where_the_money_sits.what_exists_for_other_arrondissements: Sport lines exist for at least ten arrondissements: 19e EUR 4,626,250, 13e EUR 3,818,000, 16e EUR 2,300,000, 11e EUR 1,930,000, 15e EUR 1,800,000, 10e EUR 1,010,000, 17e EUR 880,000, 12e EUR 400,000.
where_the_money_sits.what_exists_for_the_7e: For 2018 to 2022 the 7e has BPA lines under DAC, DASCO, DEVE, DPA and DVD. There is no DJS sport line in that window, which is consistent with sport being new to the 7e in the 2023 edition.
where_the_money_sits.why_this_is_not_a_finding: The autorisations de programme dataset ends at exercice 2022 and was last modified 2020-11-25. It cannot cover a 2023-edition project. The absence of a 7e sport line proves nothing about 2023.
where_the_money_sits.the_useful_part: It gives the exact budget line to ask about by name: BPA - DJS - 7e arrondissement. Asking whether that authorisation exists, and what has been engaged against it, is a precise question a Direction can answer.

why_it_may_have_stalled.note: The dataset records no reason for any operation, stalled or abandoned. What follows is signal in the data, not explanation.

signals.signal: type_financement_operation is null on both stalled operations
signals.contrast: The one operation that moved, Gym douce, carries Régie.
signals.reading: The delivery route was settled for the operation that progressed and never settled for the two that did not. An operation with no financing route recorded has not been picked up by anyone.

signals.signal: No stage date at all on either stalled operation
signals.contrast: Gym douce has debut_etudes 2024-01 and livraison_prev 2025-12.
signals.reading: They never entered studies. This is not a project that started and got stuck; it is one that never started.

signals.signal: The two stalled operations are piloted by the Direction de la Jeunesse et des Sports; the one that moved is piloted by the Direction des Espaces Verts et de l’Environnement
signals.reading: Within a single funded project, the Direction differs between what moved and what did not.

can_it_absorb_more.why: The Mairie du 7e's own page for the Budget Participatif 2023 states that this project combines three separate proposals into one. The city assembled it from three resident ideas, so absorbing a fourth element is the pattern it was built on.
can_it_absorb_more.fit: Lockers and changing serve a 2.3 km parcours sportif and a 7.7 km circuit directly. This is the missing support facility for the thing being restored, not an unrelated addition.

what_is_being_renovated.what: An existing parcours sportif that has fallen into disrepair. The public description refers to restoring the remnants of a 2.3 km sports course made of wooden apparatus and ground markings, with the renovation in wood to respect the aesthetic of the quays.
what_is_being_renovated.extent: Along quais Anatole France, from the Passerelle Léopold-Sédar-Senghor to the Pont de l'Alma.
what_is_being_renovated.why_it_matters: This changes the ask from build something new to restore something the city already owns and residents already voted to fix. That is a materially easier argument, and it means the running route already has apparatus on it.
what_is_being_renovated.source: Budget Participatif project description, read via search results. Not directly verified.

questions_to_ask: Does an autorisation de programme exist for BPA - DJS - 7e arrondissement covering the 2023 edition, and what has been engaged against it?
What is the current status of operations 7788 (Rénovation du Parcours sportif 2,3 km) and 8023 (équipements légers), neither of which has a recorded start at any stage?
The project is recorded as LIVRAISON while two of its three operations show no start. Is the remaining work still programmed, or was the project closed with those operations undelivered?
Was a financing route ever determined for those two operations? Both carry a null type_financement while the delivered operation carries Régie.
If the parcours sportif renovation proceeds, could lockers and changing be scoped into it as supporting facilities?

the_three_ideas._note: Paris publishes winning projects in open data but not the ideas residents submitted, so this list comes from the Mairie du 7e's own page rather than a dataset.

the_three_ideas.the_pattern: Three ideas went in. The one that was delivered is the seniors and gentle-exercise one, piloted by Espaces Verts. The two that never started are the two that serve runners: the 7.7 km circuit equipment and the 2.3 km quai trail. Both sit with the Direction de la Jeunesse et des Sports.
the_three_ideas.why_that_matters: It is not that the 7e failed to deliver sport. It delivered the part that fitted an existing parks programme and left the two running-specific parts unstarted. That is the gap this proposal sits in.

edition_context.note: Three winners totalling EUR 1,430,000, which matches the 2023 figure in the pipeline data exactly.

site_context_quai.water: 8 drinking fountains in the box, 2 of them on Quai Anatole France itself, both in service.
site_context_quai.toilets: 5 sanisettes, all wheelchair accessible. Two on Quai Anatole France, both open 10h00-22h00.
site_context_quai.gap_this_creates: The quai sanisettes open at 10h00, four hours later than the Champ-de-Mars ones at 06h00. For a facility aimed at people running before work, that is a real gap on this site and an argument that belongs in the proposal rather than being hidden.
site_context_quai.note: These figures are hand-checked for this record and are not yet produced by the build, unlike the Champ-de-Mars study area.
